gaps.sentence: If I were you, I ___ take the earlier train.
gaps.hint: if I were you plus would
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' is followed by 'would': would take.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: After three attempts, she ___ pass her driving test at last.
gaps.explanation: A specific past success takes 'was able to' or 'managed to': was able to pass.

gaps.sentence: The medicine ___ be kept out of the reach of children.
gaps.explanation: Written instructions use 'must' for essential requirements: must be kept.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to see that exhibition before it closes — it is outstanding.
gaps.hint: a strong recommendation with ought to
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' recommends something strongly: ought to see.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have worried — everything turned out fine.
gaps.hint: the worry was unnecessary in the end
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: We ___ hurry — the doors close in five minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' expresses urgent advice: had better hurry.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.
